screen_context._doc: Every routed screen tells Ayma what is on it: the app's ScreenCapture (ayma_flutter/lib/services/screen_capture.dart) reads the live semantics tree of the current route (route, title, headings, text, controls with id/type/state), capped and debounced, and sends it on the existing screen-context path (POST /voice/context for voice, the /chat screen_* fields for text). Widgets wrapped in NoScreenContext are never sent, NoAymaAction controls are shown but not operable, and obscured or secret fields never send their value. Routes below send nothing at all; tests in both repos fail when a route is neither captured nor listed here with a reason.

no_context.reason: start-up bootstrap; there is no signed-in session or content yet
sign-in screen: credentials and codes only, and Ayma is not running before sign-in
deleted-account recovery at sign-in; Ayma is not running before sign-in
public shared-report link opened outside a session
public page-share link opened outside a session

ui_action_policy._doc: ui_action lets Ayma tap, toggle, pick, slide, type and scroll any visible control by its id from the screen context. These rules are enforced twice: by skills/app_control.py on the label the model passes, and by the app's executor on the real control (ayma_flutter/lib/services/screen_capture.dart mirrors this block; a test checks they match). A denied control is never operated: Ayma tells the user to do it themselves (navigating there is fine). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions.

deny.say: Deleting the account or any data for good is something the user does themselves. Open the page (open_screen delete_account for the account) and tell them which button to tap.
Withdrawing face matching consent deletes the account, so the user does it themselves on the Face matching consent page (open_screen biometric_consent).
Purchases, subscriptions and credits are always the user's own tap. Open the Plan page (open_screen credits) and let them choose there.
Changing plan is a purchase, so the user does it themselves on the Plan page.
Consent is only ever the user's own tap. Tell them where to tap it.
Consent and terms checkboxes are only ever ticked by the user.
Use account_action for this; it asks the user to confirm first.
Clearing what Ayma has learned is something the user does themselves. Open the Privacy settings (open_screen privacy_settings) and tell them which button to tap.

Blocking and reporting someone is the user's own call — it affects another person and can't be undone here. Tell them it is in the menu at the top of their message thread, and let them tap it themselves.

Dismissing all suggestions at once is the user's own tap — it drops every one of them. Per-suggestion Dismiss is fine. The button is at the top of the profile suggestions (open_screen profile_suggestions).

deny_routes.reason: the face-matching consent gate must only be answered by the user
withdrawing consent deletes the account; the user acts on this page themselves
account deletion is the user's own action
the trial paywall is a purchase screen

ui_action_policy.secret_field_say: Passwords, codes and payment details are only ever typed by the user.
ui_action_policy.dialog_note: Inside a dialog or sheet whose text matches a deny pattern, every control except an escape (cancel/close/no) is denied, so Ayma never confirms a denied action.

exclusions._doc: ACTION PARITY exclusions (founder, 2026-11-06): the maintained config list of controls Ayma must NEVER activate, however she is asked. This block is the CONFIG: the command layer enforces it — account_action checks excluded_account_action_keys() (derived from the items' account_actions / destinations lists below) BEFORE dispatch and refuses a listed action however its handler field reads, ui_action refuses via ui_action_policy.deny below (mirrored in the app's screen_capture.dart), and purchase asks land on the navigate-only unavailable entry. Prompt assembly reads this same config at build time (action_facts.py renders the permitted-action context into compose_system_prompt with the exclusions applied as a filter, so a listed action never appears as permitted there either). A refusal opens the page and hands the user the exact button (the entry's say line) — it never just fails silently. The allowed side lives in destinations/settings/account_actions in this file and in docs/APP_ACTION_GRAPH.md, which marks each of these EXCLUDED. To exclude another control: add its key here, add or extend a deny rule in ui_action_policy (and the Dart mirror), make any dedicated tool path navigate-only, and update the graph — never as a one-off check inside a single tool. The system prompt (persona.md) never enumerates these buttons: it carries only a generic line that Ayma acts within her permitted action set and hands a refused action to the user (founder ruling, final form 2026-11-06).

guided_tour._doc: Ayma-DRIVEN interactive tour (ARCHITECTURE \u00a711.2b, rewired 2026-11-07): a predefined, PRIORITIZED walkthrough Ayma narrates step by step — the main features first (nav orb, the tabs, the bell), then each screen's own controls. Every step is a stop in the manifest below: 'anchor' (a tour_anchors.dart id), 'screen' (the destination key of the screen the control lives on — where Ayma navigates first when the user is not there), 'tab' (the shell IndexedStack index the anchor lives on) or 'route' (for anchors on a pushed page), 'action' ('tap' = the highlight is live; 'look' = just look), 'command' (what Ayma performs when the user taps the highlight: {action, ...args}, either 'switch_tab' with the shell tab or 'navigate' with a destination key; the client runs it through the app-command handlers and reports the confirmed outcome on tour_event, and the tour then WAITS for the user's go, Next or a spoken next; a step without one completes on the tap or Next), 'headline' and 'say' (the line Ayma speaks). LOOK-BEFORE-HIGHLIGHT: the client acks a step ok:true only when the user is actually on the step's screen and the anchor is mounted there; ok:false reason 'not_on_screen' makes the backend navigate and retry the SAME step — a step is skipped only when the client confirms the user IS on its screen but the control is genuinely absent (reason 'anchor_absent'). Started/driven by skills/guided_tour.py (start/advance/skip/back/stop) via AppCommandService 'tour_step'/'tour_end' commands + GuidedTourController. Overlay-only: no route of its own, deliberately NOT a destination/non_navigable entry — key/label/aliases below let open_screen and the deterministic matchers route 'walk me through the app' to start_guided_tour. The passive coach-mark list (tour_content.dart) is a separate first-run/new-feature mechanism and is NOT the tour.

connection_banner._doc: App-wide connection banner + client heartbeat (Nov 2026): the phone probes GET /health every 15s while foregrounded and every page shows 'Offline — showing saved data' / 'Weak connection — showing saved data' when the connection is gone or weak. Overlay-only chrome with no route, so — like guided_tour — deliberately not a destination/non_navigable entry (both are validated against the router).
connection_banner.label: Connection banner
connection_banner.reason: Ambient status chrome driven by the client heartbeat; Ayma neither opens nor changes it. If asked about it, explain what it means (the phone cannot reach, or barely reaches, the Ayma API) — never claim to fix the user's connection.

async_voice._doc: Async voice messages (Nov 2026, Chunk A): press-and-hold the chat mic (or take the offered fallback when a live call cannot connect) to record a voice message; on mic release, the clip renders in the thread immediately as a sent, playable voice bubble while uploading and processing in the background, and Ayma's spoken reply + transcript land when ready. Overlay-only chrome with no route, so — like guided_tour and connection_banner — deliberately not a destination/non_navigable entry (both are validated against the router).
async_voice.label: Voice messages
async_voice.reason: A client recording + background-delivery flow Ayma neither opens nor changes: hold the chat mic to record, release to send — the clip renders immediately as a sent, playable voice bubble, uploads in the background (queued on the phone when offline), and Ayma's spoken reply lands in the thread. If asked about it, explain how to send one; never claim to record or re-send one yourself. Playing a clip that is already in the Ayma chat is a different, covered action: use play_voice_clip (see the voice_clip_playback block).

voice_clip_playback._doc: Voice-clip playback (ACTION PARITY pilot, founder 2026-11-06, feedback items 7+8): Ayma CAN play a voice clip in the open Ayma chat — the play_voice_clip tool (skills/app_control_playback.py) queues a play_voice_clip app command and the client (AppCommandService + VoiceClipPlayback) plays it on the chat's own player. During a live voice call she announces it first, the client disconnects the session, plays the clip, then reconnects the same session with a resume note in its bootstrap context; playback never runs inside the LiveKit room, so it cannot kill the call silently. No route of its own, so — like async_voice — deliberately not a destination. This supersedes the async_voice block's old 'never play' line for clips in the Ayma chat; recording a clip as the user is still not hers to do, and DM-thread clips are not covered yet (docs/APP_ACTION_GRAPH.md GAP-2).
voice_clip_playback.label: Play a voice message

inbox_actions._doc: Inbox bulk actions (ACTION PARITY priority gaps, founder feedback items 9-11, 2026-11-06): the bulk buttons on the Notifications page and the Messages list are Ayma-operable — the tools in skills/app_control_inbox.py queue the client commands below and AppCommandService + InboxActions run the same NotificationService / DmService writes as the buttons, acking with the count that moved. set_notification_filter writes the shared NotificationFilterState the page's filter chips also write, then navigates to the page. Clear all is destructive: Ayma confirms with the user in conversation before calling it (her tool description carries that rule), the same check the button's dialog performs. No route of their own, so — like voice_clip_playback — deliberately not destinations.
inbox_actions.label: Inbox bulk actions (notifications and messages)

voice_call_resilience._doc: Forgiving voice-call route (Nov 2026): if a voice call's first connect attempt fails, the app retries once with WebRTC forced onto LiveKit Cloud TURN relay (TLS/443), which survives UDP-blocking and weak networks; the status line reads 'Reconnecting…' during the retry. If an established call's connection drops mid-call, the LiveKit SDK re-establishes it and resumes the same session — the voice status reads 'Reconnecting…' while that lasts and the call only ends if the reconnect ultimately fails. Behavior inside the existing voice-call feature with no route of its own, so — like connection_banner — deliberately not a destination/non_navigable entry (both are validated against the router).
voice_call_resilience.label: Voice call reconnecting
aliases: why does my call keep reconnecting
voice_call_resilience.reason: Automatic client behavior in the voice transport/controller; Ayma neither triggers nor configures it. If asked about it, explain what it means (the phone's connection dropped and the call is re-establishing itself over a more forgiving route) — never claim to fix the user's connection.

offline_first._doc: Offline-first rendering (Nov 2026): the main screens paint their last-known content from the on-device cache the moment they open, then refresh from the network behind it — no full-screen loading spinner when any saved content exists. The Explore feed's first page and the Plan page snapshot persist per-account in the report cache (wiped on sign-out); Firestore-backed surfaces (messages, DMs, notifications, profile) read their on-device Firestore cache first by construction. Behavior inside existing screens with no route of its own, so — like connection_banner — deliberately not a destination/non_navigable entry (both are validated against the router).
offline_first.label: Offline-first / saved content
aliases: why can i see old data
offline_first.reason: Automatic client behavior (stale-while-revalidate caches); Ayma neither triggers nor configures it. If asked about it, explain what it means (the app shows the last content it saved on this phone and refreshes it when the connection allows) — never claim the saved content is current.

voice_entry_degrade._doc: Voice-entry degrade glue (Nov 2026, resilience chunk D): every live-voice entry point (chat mic, nav-bar orb, practice calls) consults the connection heartbeat before attempting a call. Offline: no attempt is made — the user gets a clear note and (in chat) the voice-message offer instead. Weak: the call starts on the forgiving TURN-relay route from the first attempt instead of spending it on the direct route. If one live session drops and re-establishes twice, the chat offers a one-tap switch of that conversation to a voice message. Behavior layered on the existing voice features with no route of its own, so — like connection_banner — deliberately not a destination/non_navigable entry (both are validated against the router).
voice_entry_degrade.label: Voice offline and weak-connection handling
voice_entry_degrade.reason: Automatic client behavior driven by the connection heartbeat; Ayma neither triggers nor configures it. If asked about it, explain what it means (the phone's connection is too weak or absent for a live call, so the app protects the conversation by offering a voice message instead) — never claim to fix the user's connection.

navigation._doc: Session navigation memory (founder feedback item 15): the app keeps a session-only stack of the pages the user has been on — their own navigation and Ayma-driven opens alike — in ayma_flutter/lib/services/navigation_history.dart, capped at 20 entries and never persisted. Ayma's screen context carries the current page and the previous page's spoken label. The one action below unwinds one step per call; a modal/sheet is dismissed first (as the user's own back would), an active tour blocks it, and at the root it answers honestly instead of failing silently or exiting.
